paragraphs: Infinite Campus sells a student information system to school districts, and says the system carries more than 1500 core tools. Add-on products are built to work with that system instead of leaning on third-party software. Customers include school districts, regional consortia, state departments of education and the federal government.

The system takes on time-consuming administrative work such as student enrollment, scheduling, attendance and grading. Products added over the years include food service, online payments, online registration and messaging. Cross-Site Enrollment lets a student take a class at another school in the district, or at another district in the same state that uses the system. The company says it updates the product monthly with new functionality.

The company was founded in 1993 by Charlie Kratsch. It is headquartered in Blaine, Minnesota. It reports more than 650 employees, including over 300 in-house developers. It says it is free from outside investors and the revenue pressure that comes with them. It describes one system used by more than 3,200 districts. It also reports a district renewal rate above 99% every year.
